overview: School Committee Vice Chair Jenny Graham reviewed the school district's budget process, municipal reserve funds, and the Medford High School building project with the Massachusetts School Building Authority. She also previewed three upcoming November ballot questions regarding operational overrides and a debt exclusion.

items.title: Introduction and Local Dining
items.summary: Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan opened the podcast, and School Committee Vice Chair Jenny Graham highlighted recent additions at local restaurant AltaCuba.

items.title: School District Budget Season and Policy Codification
items.summary: Graham discussed how the School Committee codified its budget and capital planning policies to start earlier in the fiscal year, navigated the expiration of federal ESSER funds, and avoided deeper cuts by restoring several administrative and instructional positions.

items.title: Free Cash and Stabilization Reserves
items.summary: Graham explained that free cash functions as a non-recurring rainy day reserve rather than sustainable operating revenue, noting that the City Council transferred $3 million for a school feasibility study and $11 million into stabilization accounts.

items.title: High School Building Project and MSBA Eligibility Phase
items.summary: Graham reported that the building committee completed and submitted its educational profile, enrollment projections, and vocational documentation to the Massachusetts School Building Authority ahead of deadline, clearing the path to procure an owner's project manager and architect.

items.title: November Proposition 2½ Ballot Questions
items.summary: Graham outlined the three November ballot questions, which include a debt exclusion for a new fire station, an operational override supporting schools and DPW infrastructure, and dedicated school funding aimed at pay equity for paraprofessionals and support staff.
